sanskrit: krodho bhedo bhayo daṇḍaḥ karśanaṃ nigraho vadhaḥ nayanty arivaśaṃ sadyo gaṇān bharatasattama
english: Wrath, division, terror, the rod of punishment, oppression, coercion, and slaughter swiftly lead confederacies under the enemy's sway, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tasmān mānayitavyās te gaṇamukhyāḥ pradhānataḥ lokayātrā samāyattā bhūyasī teṣu pārthiva
english: Therefore the chiefs of the confederacy must above all be honored, for upon them, O son of Pṛthā, the greater course of worldly affairs depends.

sanskrit: mantraguptiḥ pradhāneṣu cāraś cāmitrakarśana na gaṇāḥ kṛtsnaśo mantraṃ śrotum arhanti bhārata
english: The keeping of counsel rests with the leading men, as does espionage, O crusher of foes; not the whole confederacy is fit to hear the secret counsel, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gaṇamukhyais tu saṃbhūya kāryaṃ gaṇahitaṃ mithaḥ pṛthag gaṇasya bhinnasya vimatasya tato 'nyathā arthāḥ pratyavasīdanti tathānarthā bhavanti ca
english: Coming together with the chiefs of the confederacy, what serves its common good must be done in concert; but when the confederacy is split apart and divided in mind, its interests sink to ruin and misfortunes arise.

sanskrit: teṣām anyonyabhinnānāṃ svaśaktim anutiṣṭhatām nigrahaḥ paṇḍitaiḥ kāryaḥ kṣipram eva pradhānataḥ
english: When they are divided one against another, each pursuing his own power, the wise must restrain them at once, and the leading men above all.

sanskrit: kuleṣu kalahā jātāḥ kulavṛddhair upekṣitāḥ gotrasya rājan kurvanti gaṇasaṃbhedakārikām
english: Quarrels that arise within the clans, when neglected by the clan-elders, O king, bring about the very thing that shatters the confederacy of the lineage.

sanskrit: ābhyantaraṃ bhayaṃ rakṣyaṃ surakṣyaṃ bāhyato bhayam abhyantarād bhayaṃ jātaṃ sadyo mūlaṃ nikṛntati
english: The inner danger must be guarded against, the danger from without warded off with care; for danger born from within cuts away the very root in an instant.

sanskrit: akasmāt krodhalobhād vā mohād vāpi svabhāvajāt anyonyaṃ nābhibhāṣante tat parābhavalakṣaṇam
english: When, from sudden wrath or greed, or from delusion sprung of their own nature, men cease to speak to one another, that is the mark of impending ruin.

sanskrit: jātyā ca sadṛśāḥ sarve kulena sadṛśās tathā na tu śauryeṇa buddhyā vā rūpadravyeṇa vā punaḥ
english: In birth all are equal, and likewise equal in lineage; yet not so in valor, nor in intellect, nor again in beauty or in wealth.

sanskrit: bhedāc caiva pramādāc ca nāmyante ripubhir gaṇāḥ tasmāt saṃghātam evāhur gaṇānāṃ śaraṇaṃ mahat
english: Through division and through heedlessness confederacies are bent low by their foes; therefore men declare that union alone is the great refuge of confederacies.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mahān ayaṃ dharmapatho bahuśākhaś ca bhārata kiṃ svid eveha dharmāṇām anuṣṭheyatamaṃ matam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Great is this path of dharma, O Bhārata, and many-branched; which among all the duties is held to be the most worthy of being practiced here?

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ garīyo bhavato matam yathāyaṃ puruṣo dharmam iha ca pretya cāpnuyāt
english: What deed, in your judgment, is weightier than all duties, whereby a man may attain to dharma both here and in the world beyond?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mātāpitror gurūṇāṃ ca pūjā bahumatā mama atra yukto naro lokān yaśaś ca mahad aśnute
english: Bhīṣma said: The worship of mother and father and of teachers I hold in highest esteem; the man devoted to this wins the worlds and great renown.

sanskrit: yad ete hy abhijānīyuḥ karma tāta supūjitāḥ dharmyaṃ dharmaviruddhaṃ vā tat kartavyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Whatever deed these, well-honored, may command, my son—whether it accord with dharma or seem against it—that must be done, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: na tair anabhyanujñāto dharmam anyaṃ prakalpayet yam ete 'bhyanujānīyuḥ sa dharma iti niścayaḥ
english: Without their leave one should ordain no other duty for oneself; that which these sanction is, by firm conviction, dharma itself.

sanskrit: eta eva trayo lokā eta evāśramās trayaḥ eta eva trayo vedā eta eva trayo 'gnayaḥ
english: These very three are the three worlds; these very ones the three āśramas; these very ones the three Vedas; these very ones the three sacred fires.

sanskrit: pitā hy agnir gārhapatyo mātāgnir dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ gurur āhavanīyas tu sāgnitretā garīyasī
english: The father is the Gārhapatya fire, the mother is remembered as the Dakṣiṇa fire, and the teacher is the Āhavanīya; this triad of fires is the most venerable.

sanskrit: triṣv apramādyann eteṣu trīṃl lokān avajeṣyasi pitṛvṛttyā tv imaṃ lokaṃ mātṛvṛttyā tathāparam brahmalokaṃ guror vṛttyā nityam eva cariṣyasi
english: Being heedful toward these three, you shall conquer the three worlds: by serving the father this world, by serving the mother the next, and by serving the teacher you shall ever walk in the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: samyag eteṣu vartasva triṣu lokeṣu bhārata yaśaḥ prāpsyasi bhadraṃ te dharmaṃ ca sumahāphalam
english: Conduct yourself rightly toward these three, O Bhārata; in the three worlds you shall win renown—blessings upon you—and dharma of most abundant fruit.

sanskrit: naitān atiśayej jātu nātyaśnīyān na dūṣayet nityaṃ paricarec caiva tad vai sukṛtam uttamam kīrtiṃ puṇyaṃ yaśo lokān prāpsyase ca janādhipa
english: One should never surpass them, never eat before them, never wrong them, but ever attend upon them; that indeed is the highest good deed, and thereby, O lord of men, you shall gain fame, merit, glory, and the heavenly worlds.

sanskrit: sarve tasyādṛtā lokā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ anādṛtās tu yasyaite sarvās tasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ
english: For him by whom these three are honored, all worlds are honored; but for him by whom these are unhonored, all rites bear no fruit.

sanskrit: naivāyaṃ na paro lokas tasya caiva paraṃtapa amānitā nityam eva yasyaite guravas trayaḥ
english: Neither this world nor the world beyond belongs to him, O scorcher of foes, by whom these three venerable ones are ever left unhonored.

sanskrit: na cāsmin na pare loke yaśas tasya prakāśate na cānyad api kalyāṇaṃ pāratraṃ samudāhṛtam
english: Neither in this world nor in the next does his fame shine forth, nor is any other blessing declared to await him hereafter.

sanskrit: tebhya eva tu tat sarvaṃ kṛtyayā visṛjāmy aham tad āsīn me śataguṇaṃ sahasraguṇam eva ca tasmān me saṃprakāśante trayo lokā yudhiṣṭhira
english: To these very ones I render up all my labor in deed; thereby it became for me a hundredfold and a thousandfold, and so, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the three worlds shine open before me.

sanskrit: daśaiva tu sadācāryaḥ śrotriyān atiricyate daśācāryān upādhyāya upādhyāyān pitā daśa
english: A teacher of good conduct surpasses ten learned reciters of the Veda; a preceptor surpasses ten such teachers; and a father ten preceptors.

sanskrit: pitṝn daśa tu mātaikā sarvāṃ vā pṛthivīm api gurutvenābhibhavati nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ gurur garīyān pitṛto mātṛtaś ceti me matiḥ
english: But one mother surpasses ten fathers, or even the whole earth, in the weight of her venerableness; there is no elder equal to the mother. Yet the teacher is weightier than both father and mother—such is my conviction.

sanskrit: ubhau hi mātāpitarau janmani vyupayujyataḥ śarīram etau sṛjataḥ pitā mātā ca bhārata ācāryaśiṣṭā yā jātiḥ sā divyā sājarāmarā
english: Both mother and father join together in one's birth; father and mother fashion the body, O Bhārata; but the second birth shaped by the teacher's instruction is divine, free from age and death.

sanskrit: avadhyā hi sadā mātā pitā cāpy apakāriṇau na saṃduṣyati tat kṛtvā na ca te dūṣayanti tam dharmāya yatamānānāṃ vidur devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ
english: Mother and father are ever inviolable, even when they do one wrong; he who acts thus is not defiled, nor do they defile him. The gods, together with the seers, know those who strive for dharma.

sanskrit: ya āvṛṇoty avitathena karṇāv; ṛtaṃ bruvann amṛtaṃ saṃprayacchan taṃ vai manye pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca; tasmai na druhyet kṛtam asya jānan
english: He who fills one's ears with what is true, speaking the right and bestowing the deathless—him I deem both father and mother; against him one should never bear malice, knowing what he has done.

sanskrit: vidyāṃ śrutvā ye guruṃ nādriyante; pratyāsannaṃ manasā karmaṇā vā yathaiva te gurubhir bhāvanīyās; tathā teṣāṃ guravo 'py arcanīyāḥ
english: They who, having heard knowledge, do not revere the teacher close at hand, in thought or in deed—just as they ought to be regarded by their teachers, so too must their teachers be honored by them.

sanskrit: tasmāt pūjayitavyāś ca saṃvibhajyāś ca yatnataḥ guravo 'rcayitavyāś ca purāṇaṃ dharmam icchatā
english: Therefore the teachers must be worshiped, and shared with diligently, and honored, by one who desires the ancient dharma.

sanskrit: yena prītāś ca pitaras tena prītaḥ pitāmahaḥ prīṇāti mātaraṃ yena pṛthivī tena pūjitā
english: By whatever pleases the fathers, the grandfather too is pleased; by whatever delights the mother, the earth herself is honored.

sanskrit: yena prīṇāty upādhyāyaṃ tena syād brahma pūjitam mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaś caiva tasmāt pūjyatamo guruḥ ṛṣayaś ca hi devāś ca prīyante pitṛbhiḥ saha
english: By whatever pleases the preceptor, Brahman itself is worshiped; therefore the teacher is more worthy of worship than mother and father alike; and the seers and the gods, together with the ancestors, are gladdened thereby.

sanskrit: na kena cana vṛttena hy avajñeyo gurur bhavet na ca mātā na ca pitā tādṛśo yādṛśo guruḥ
english: By no manner of conduct should the teacher ever be despised; nor is the mother, nor the father, such as the teacher is.

sanskrit: na te 'vamānam arhanti na ca te dūṣayanti tam gurūṇām eva satkāraṃ vidur devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ
english: They deserve no contempt, nor do they defile him; the gods, together with the seers, acknowledge the honoring of teachers as supreme.

sanskrit: upādhyāyaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca; ye 'bhidruhyanti manasā karmaṇā vā teṣāṃ pāpaṃ bhrūṇahatyāviśiṣṭaṃ; tasmān nānyaḥ pāpakṛd asti loke
english: They who do violence to preceptor, father, or mother, in thought or in deed—their sin is greater than the slaying of an unborn child; than they there is no worse doer of evil in the world.

sanskrit: mitradruhaḥ kṛtaghnasya strīghnasya piśunasya ca caturṇāṃ vayam eteṣāṃ niṣkṛtiṃ nānuśuśrumaḥ
english: For the betrayer of a friend, the ingrate, the slayer of a woman, and the slanderer—for these four we have never heard of any expiation.

sanskrit: etat sarvam atideśena sṛṣṭaṃ; yat kartavyaṃ puruṣeṇeha loke etac chreyo nānyad asmād viśiṣṭaṃ; sarvān dharmān anusṛtyaitad uktam
english: All this has been set forth by way of injunction, as what a man ought to do here in the world; this is the highest good, and nothing surpasses it; surveying every duty, this has been declared.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ dharme sthātum icchan naro varteta bhārata vidvañ jijñāsamānāya prabrūhi bharatarṣabha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How should a man conduct himself who wishes to abide in dharma, O Bhārata? Learned one, declare it to me who would know, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: satyaṃ caivānṛtaṃ cobhe lokān āvṛtya tiṣṭhataḥ tayoḥ kim ācared rājan puruṣo dharmaniścitaḥ
english: Both truth and falsehood stand pervading the worlds; of the two, O king, which should a man resolved upon dharma practice?

sanskrit: kiṃ svit satyaṃ kim anṛtaṃ kiṃ svid dharmyaṃ sanātanam kasmin kāle vadet satyaṃ kasmin kāle 'nṛtaṃ vadet
english: What is truth, what is falsehood, and what is the eternal accord with dharma? At what time should one speak the truth, and at what time should one utter what is false?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca satyasya vacanaṃ sādhu na satyād vidyate param yad bhūloke sudurjñātaṃ tat te vakṣyāmi bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: The speaking of truth is good; nothing is higher than truth. Yet that which in this earthly world is most hard to discern, that I shall tell you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhavet satyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ vaktavyam anṛtaṃ bhavet yatrānṛtaṃ bhavet satyaṃ satyaṃ vāpy anṛtaṃ bhavet
english: There are times when truth should not be spoken and falsehood ought to be uttered, where falsehood becomes truth and truth becomes falsehood.

sanskrit: tādṛśe muhyate bālo yatra satyam aniṣṭhitam satyānṛte viniścitya tato bhavati dharmavit
english: In such a case the fool is bewildered, where truth is not fixed; only after discerning truth and falsehood does one become a knower of dharma.

sanskrit: apy anāryo 'kṛtaprajñaḥ puruṣo 'pi sudāruṇaḥ sumahat prāpnuyāt puṇyaṃ balāko 'ndhavadhād iva
english: Even a man ignoble, of unripe wisdom, and most cruel may attain great merit—as Balāka did by the slaying of a blind creature.

sanskrit: kim āścaryaṃ ca yan mūḍho dharmakāmo 'py adharmavit sumahat prāpnuyāt pāpaṃ gaṅgāyām iva kauśikaḥ
english: And what wonder is it that a deluded man, though desiring dharma yet ignorant of it, may incur great sin—as Kauśika did at the Gaṅgā?

sanskrit: tādṛśo 'yam anupraśno yatra dharmaḥ sudurvacaḥ duṣkaraḥ pratisaṃkhyātuṃ tarkeṇātra vyavasyati
english: Such is this further question, wherein dharma is most hard to declare and hard to reckon; here one must determine it by reasoning.

sanskrit: prabhāvārthāya bhūtānāṃ dharmapravacanaṃ kṛtam yat syād ahiṃsāsaṃyuktaṃ sa dharma iti niścayaḥ
english: The teaching of dharma was made for the welfare of beings; that which is joined with non-injury is dharma—such is the firm conclusion.

sanskrit: dhāraṇād dharma ity āhur dharmeṇa vidhṛtāḥ prajāḥ yat syād dhāraṇasaṃyuktaṃ sa dharma iti niścayaḥ
english: From its upholding they call it dharma; by dharma are creatures upheld; that which is joined with upholding is dharma—such is the firm conclusion.

sanskrit: śrutidharma iti hy eke nety āhur apare janāḥ na tu tat pratyasūyāmo na hi sarvaṃ vidhīyate
english: Some say dharma is that which the scripture enjoins; others deny it. Yet we do not cavil at this, for not everything is laid down by rule.

sanskrit: ye 'nyāyena jihīrṣanto dhanam icchanti karhi cit tebhyas tan na tad ākhyeyaṃ sa dharma iti niścayaḥ
english: To those who, seeking to seize wealth unjustly, ever covet it, that should not be disclosed; that is dharma—such is the firm conclusion.

sanskrit: akūjanena cen mokṣo nātra kūjet kathaṃ cana avaśyaṃ kūjitavyaṃ vā śaṅkeran vāpy akūjanāt
english: If by silence there be escape, here one should by no means speak; or if one must needs speak, or if his silence would arouse suspicion, then let him speak.

sanskrit: śreyas tatrānṛtaṃ vaktuṃ satyād iti vicāritam yaḥ pāpaiḥ saha saṃbandhān mucyate śapathād iti
english: There it is judged better to speak falsehood than truth, whereby one is freed from dealings with the wicked, even by a false oath.

sanskrit: na ca tebhyo dhanaṃ deyaṃ śakye sati kathaṃ cana pāpebhyo hi dhanaṃ dattaṃ dātāram api pīḍayet
english: And to such men no wealth should be given, by any means, so long as it can be helped; for wealth given to the wicked torments even the giver.

sanskrit: svaśarīroparodhena varam ādātum icchataḥ satyasaṃpratipattyarthaṃ ye brūyuḥ sākṣiṇaḥ kva cit anuktvā tatra tad vācyaṃ sarve te 'nṛtavādinaḥ
english: When one is willing to seize a boon even at the cost of his own life, those witnesses who, to establish the truth, would speak there—if they leave that unsaid which ought to be said, all of them are speakers of falsehood.

sanskrit: prāṇātyaye vivāhe ca vaktavyam anṛtaṃ bhavet arthasya rakṣaṇārthāya pareṣāṃ dharmakāraṇāt pareṣāṃ dharmam ākāṅkṣan nīcaḥ syād dharmabhikṣukaḥ
english: In peril of life and in marriage, falsehood ought to be spoken, for the safeguarding of wealth and for the sake of another's dharma; yet he who, craving others' dharma, would beg it as alms becomes base.

sanskrit: pratiśrutya tu dātavyaṃ śvaḥkāryas tu balātkṛtaḥ yaḥ kaś cid dharmasamayāt pracyuto 'dharmam āsthitaḥ
english: Having promised, one must give; but he who is coerced may put it off to the morrow. Whoever has fallen from the compact of dharma and taken his stand in unrighteousness—

sanskrit: śaṭhaḥ svadharmam utsṛjya tam icched upajīvitum sarvopāyair nihantavyaḥ pāpo nikṛtijīvanaḥ
english: that knave who, casting off his own dharma, would seek to live by deceit—such a sinner, living by treachery, must be destroyed by every means.

sanskrit: dhanam ity eva pāpānāṃ sarveṣām iha niścayaḥ ye 'viṣahyā hy asaṃbhojyā nikṛtyā patanaṃ gatāḥ
english: 'Wealth, and wealth alone'—such is the resolve of all the wicked here, who are insufferable, unfit to dine with, and through their treachery sunk into ruin.

sanskrit: cyutā devamanuṣyebhyo yathā pretās tathaiva te dhanādānād duḥkhataraṃ jīvitād viprayojanam
english: Fallen away from gods and men, they are even as the departed dead; yet harder to bear for them than the seizing of their wealth is to be parted from life.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vo rocatāṃ dharma iti vācyaḥ prayatnataḥ na kaś cid asti pāpānāṃ dharma ity eṣa niścayaḥ
english: 'Let this dharma find favor with you'—so should one earnestly speak to them; for there is no dharma among the wicked—such is the firm conclusion.

sanskrit: tathāgataṃ ca yo hanyān nāsau pāpena lipyate svakarmaṇā hataṃ hanti hata eva sa hanyate teṣu yaḥ samayaṃ kaś cit kurvīta hatabuddhiṣu
english: He who slays one brought to such a pass is not smeared with sin; he slays one already slain by his own deeds; that man, already as good as dead, is but slain. Whoever would make any pact with those of ruined understanding—

sanskrit: yathā kākaś ca gṛdhraś ca tathaivopadhijīvinaḥ ūrdhvaṃ dehavimokṣānte bhavanty etāsu yoniṣu
english: As crows and as vultures, so too those who live by fraud—at the last release of the body they are reborn into such wombs as these.

sanskrit: yasmin yathā vartate yo manuṣyas; tasmiṃs tathā vartitavyaṃ sa dharmaḥ māyācāro māyayā vartitavyaḥ; sādhvācāraḥ sādhunā pratyudeyaḥ
english: As a man behaves toward another, so toward him one ought to behave—that is dharma: against the man of guile one must act with guile, and the man of good conduct must be met with goodness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kliśyamāneṣu bhūteṣu tais tair bhāvais tatas tataḥ durgāṇy atitared yena tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When beings are afflicted by this and that condition on every side, tell me, grandfather, by what means one may cross over these hard straits.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca āśrameṣu yathokteṣu yathoktaṃ ye dvijātayaḥ vartante saṃyatātmāno durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Bhīṣma said: Those twice-born who conduct themselves as prescribed within the prescribed stages of life, with selves restrained—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: ye dambhān na japanti sma yeṣāṃ vṛttiś ca saṃvṛtā viṣayāṃś ca nigṛhṇanti durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who do not mutter prayers out of hypocrisy, whose livelihood is well-ordered, and who curb the objects of sense—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: vāsayanty atithīn nityaṃ nityaṃ ye cānasūyakāḥ nityaṃ svādhyāyaśīlāś ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who ever lodge their guests, who are ever free from envy, and ever devoted to the study of the Veda—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: mātāpitroś ca ye vṛttiṃ vartante dharmakovidāḥ varjayanti divāsvapnaṃ durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They, skilled in dharma, who attend upon mother and father, and who shun sleeping by day—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: sveṣu dāreṣu vartante nyāyavṛtteṣv ṛtāv ṛtau agnihotraparāḥ santo durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who go to their own wives, righteous in conduct, each in her due season, and who are devoted to the fire-oblation—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: ye na lobhān nayanty arthān rājāno rajasāvṛtāḥ viṣayān parirakṣanto durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those kings who do not exact wealth through greed, though wrapped in passion, but guard their realms—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: āhaveṣu ca ye śūrās tyaktvā maraṇajaṃ bhayam dharmeṇa jayam icchanto durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those heroes in battle who, casting aside the fear born of death, seek victory by righteous means—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: ye pāpāni na kurvanti karmaṇā manasā girā nikṣiptadaṇḍā bhūteṣu durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who do no evil in deed, in thought, or in word, who have laid down the rod against living beings—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: ye vadantīha satyāni prāṇatyāge 'py upasthite pramāṇabhūtā bhūtānāṃ durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who speak the truth here even when the loss of life is at hand, who stand as a measure of conduct for all beings—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: anadhyāyeṣu ye viprāḥ svādhyāyaṃ naiva kurvate taponityāḥ sutapaso durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those brāhmaṇas who do not pursue Vedic recitation on the days when study is forbidden, who are ever given to austerity and of noble penance—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: karmāṇy akuhakārthāni yeṣāṃ vācaś ca sūnṛtāḥ yeṣām arthāś ca sādhvarthā durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They whose deeds are without trickery of purpose, whose words are kind and true, and whose aims are aims of the good—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: ye tapaś ca tapasyanti kaumārabrahmacāriṇaḥ vidyāvedavratasnātā durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who practice austerity, chaste from boyhood, who have completed their bath of learning, Veda, and vows—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: ye ca saṃśāntarajasaḥ saṃśāntatamasaś ca ye satye sthitā mahātmāno durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They in whom the passion of rajas is wholly stilled and the darkness of tamas wholly quenched, great souls established in truth—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ na kaś cit trasati trasanti na ca kasya cit yeṣām ātmasamo loko durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They of whom none is afraid and who fear none, to whom the world is even as their own self—they cross over the hard straits.

sanskrit: paraśriyā na tapyante ye santaḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ grāmyād annān nivṛttāś ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those good men, those bulls among men, who are not tormented by another's fortune, and who have turned away from coarse village food—they cross over the hard straits.
